scope: Leviticus 11–12, all 55 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Leviticus 11–12. Full original XML records include the written/read note at 11:21 and large-letter annotation at 11:42.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps both recipients of the divine speech, not the usual Moses-only formula.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying to them,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying to them,

verses.rationale: Unfolds collective animal language as a natural heading while retaining terrestrial scope and permission.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: These are the living creatures you may eat among all the animals on the earth.
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: These are the land animals you may eat.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: These are the living creatures you may eat among all the animals on the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps both required conditions and the emphatic split-hoof description rather than treating either condition as sufficient.
verses.before: Any animal that has a divided hoof, completely split, and chews the cud—you may eat.
verses.after: You may eat any animal that has hooves completely split in two and chews the cud.
verses.tsw_comparator: Any animal that has a divided hoof, completely split, and chews the cud—you may eat.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exception list, camel and source observation without substituting modern zoological categories.
verses.before: But among those that chew the cud or have a divided hoof, you will not eat these: the camel, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean to you.
verses.after: But these animals that chew the cud or have divided hooves must not be eaten. The camel chews the cud but does not have divided hooves; it is unclean to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But among those that chew the cud or have a divided hoof, you shall not eat these: the camel, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean to you.

verses.rationale: Uses rock hyrax for shaphan, retaining the source’s cud description and repeated unclean-to-you conclusion.
verses.before: The rock badger, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean to you.
verses.after: The rock hyrax chews the cud but does not have divided hooves; it is unclean to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: The rock badger, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean to you.

verses.rationale: Retains hare and source description without silently correcting it to modern digestive classification.
verses.before: The hare, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean to you.
verses.after: The hare chews the cud but does not have divided hooves; it is unclean to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: The hare, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps pig’s reverse combination of traits and repeated classification.
verses.before: The pig, because it has a divided hoof, completely split, but does not chew the cud; it is unclean to you.
verses.after: The pig has hooves completely split in two but does not chew the cud; it is unclean to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: The pig, because it has a divided hoof, completely split, but does not chew the cud; it is unclean to you.

verses.rationale: Preserves separate eating and carcass-contact prohibitions and repeated relational classification.
verses.before: You will not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses. They are unclean to you.
verses.after: Do not eat their meat or touch their carcasses. They are unclean to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses. They are unclean to you.

verses.rationale: Retains both required features and both water settings without narrowing all water creatures to fish.
verses.before: These you may eat from everything in the waters: whatever has fins and scales in the waters, whether in seas or rivers, you may eat.
verses.after: Of the creatures living in water, you may eat any that have fins and scales, whether in the seas or the streams.
verses.tsw_comparator: These you may eat from everything in the waters: whatever has fins and scales in the waters, whether in seas or rivers, you may eat.

verses.rationale: Preserves comprehensive aquatic scope, swarming and living categories, and detestable rather than replacing it with unclean.
verses.before: But whatever does not have fins and scales in the seas and rivers, among all that swarm in the waters and every living creature in the waters, will be detestable to you.
verses.after: But anything in the seas or streams that does not have both fins and scales—whether among the swarming creatures or any other living creature in the water—is detestable to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But whatever does not have fins and scales in the seas and rivers, among all that swarm in the waters and every living creature in the waters, shall be detestable to you.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated detestation language and distinct meat/carcass instructions.
verses.before: They will be detestable to you; you will not eat their flesh, and you will detest their carcasses.
verses.after: You must regard them as detestable. Do not eat their meat, and regard their carcasses as detestable.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall be detestable to you; you shall not eat their flesh, and you shall detest their carcasses.

verses.rationale: Keeps the summary repeated from earlier rule rather than removing it as redundancy.
verses.before: Whatever in the waters has no fins and scales will be detestable to you.
verses.after: Anything in the water that does not have both fins and scales is detestable to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whatever in the waters has no fins and scales shall be detestable to you.

verses.rationale: Preserves prohibition and first three named creatures, with eagle/vulture identification uncertainty recorded in notes and flying category encompassing bat.
verses.before: These you will detest among the birds; they will not be eaten, for they are detestable: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
verses.after: Among flying creatures, regard these as detestable; they must not be eaten: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
verses.tsw_comparator: These you shall detest among the birds; they shall not be eaten, for they are detestable: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,

verses.rationale: Keeps two Hebrew names and kind qualifier on the second; exact raptor identifications remain provisional.
verses.before: the kite and every kind of falcon,
verses.after: the kite, every kind of falcon,
verses.tsw_comparator: the kite and every kind of falcon,

verses.rationale: Retains the entire raven category within the continuing list.
verses.before: every kind of raven,
verses.after: every kind of raven,
verses.tsw_comparator: every kind of raven,

verses.rationale: Keeps four source names and hawk-kind qualifier; notes significant owl/ostrich alternative and uncertainty.
verses.before: the ostrich, the night hawk, the sea gull, and every kind of hawk,
verses.after: the ostrich, the nighthawk, the gull, every kind of hawk,
verses.tsw_comparator: the ostrich, the night hawk, the sea gull, and every kind of hawk,

verses.rationale: Preserves three names in order using provisional traditional identifications rather than omitting uncertain species.
verses.before: the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
verses.after: the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
verses.tsw_comparator: the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,

verses.rationale: Keeps three distinct entries, while apparatus warns that exact species assignments are uncertain.
verses.before: the white owl, the desert owl, the carrion vulture,
verses.after: the barn owl, the pelican, the carrion vulture,
verses.tsw_comparator: the white owl, the desert owl, the carrion vulture,

verses.rationale: Retains four entries, heron-kind scope and bat within the ancient flying-creature category.
verses.before: the stork, every kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
verses.after: the stork, every kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
verses.tsw_comparator: the stork, every kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.

verses.rationale: Preserves source locomotion classification and detestable judgment without modernizing to a six-legged taxonomy.
verses.before: Every winged swarming creature that walks on four legs will be detestable to you.
verses.after: Every winged swarming creature that goes on all fours is detestable to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every winged swarming creature that walks on four legs shall be detestable to you.

verses.rationale: Follows qere to-it/has over written not, preserves exception and raised jumping-leg feature; full original note is hashed.
verses.before: Yet among all winged swarming creatures that walk on four legs, you may eat those that have jointed legs above their feet for leaping on the ground.
verses.after: Yet among the winged swarming creatures that go on all fours, you may eat those with jointed legs above their feet for leaping on the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet among all winged swarming creatures that walk on four legs, you may eat those that have jointed legs above their feet for leaping on the ground.

verses.rationale: Preserves four named insect groups and each kind scope, with identifications explicitly provisional in notes.
verses.before: Of these you may eat every kind of locust, every kind of bald locust, every kind of cricket, and every kind of grasshopper.
verses.after: You may eat these: every kind of locust, bald locust, cricket, and grasshopper.
verses.tsw_comparator: Of these you may eat every kind of locust, every kind of bald locust, every kind of cricket, and every kind of grasshopper.

verses.rationale: Retains four-leg language and supplies other from the preceding permitted exception.
verses.before: But every other winged swarming creature that has four legs will be detestable to you.
verses.after: But every other winged swarming creature with four legs is detestable to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But every other winged swarming creature that has four legs shall be detestable to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps transition to contact impurity and exact evening endpoint, continuing to carrying rule.
verses.before: By these you will become unclean: whoever touches their carcass will be unclean until evening,
verses.after: These creatures make you unclean: anyone who touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening,
verses.tsw_comparator: By these you shall become unclean: whoever touches their carcass shall be unclean until evening,

verses.rationale: Preserves any-part scope and clothes-washing requirement for carrying, distinct from touching alone.
verses.before: and whoever carries any part of their carcass will wash their clothes and be unclean until evening.
verses.after: and anyone who carries any part of their carcasses must wash their clothes and remain unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: and whoever carries any part of their carcass shall wash their clothes and be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Retains hoofed description, source conjunction and both failures; notes the touch context is carcasses, not an invented general ban on living animals.
verses.before: Every animal that has a divided hoof but is not completely split, or does not chew the cud, is unclean to you. Whoever touches one will be unclean.
verses.after: Any hoofed animal whose hooves are not fully split and that does not chew the cud is unclean to you. Anyone who touches them becomes unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every animal that has a divided hoof but is not completely split, or does not chew the cud, is unclean to you. Whoever touches one shall be unclean.

verses.rationale: Keeps paws versus hoof distinction and explicit carcass contact, with evening duration.
verses.before: Whatever walks on paws among all animals that walk on four legs is unclean to you. Whoever touches their carcass will be unclean until evening.
verses.after: Among animals that go on all fours, all that walk on paws are unclean to you. Anyone who touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whatever walks on paws among all animals that walk on four legs is unclean to you. Whoever touches their carcass shall be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Preserves carrying/washing rule and repeated categorical conclusion.
verses.before: Whoever carries their carcass will wash their clothes and be unclean until evening. They are unclean to you.
verses.after: Anyone who carries their carcasses must wash their clothes and remain unclean until evening. They are unclean to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever carries their carcass shall wash their clothes and be unclean until evening. They are unclean to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps three named groups and qualifier on last, with uncertain rodent/lizard identifications acknowledged.
verses.before: These are unclean to you among the swarming creatures that swarm on the ground: the weasel, the mouse, every kind of great lizard,
verses.after: Among the creatures that swarm on the ground, these are unclean to you: the weasel, the mouse, every kind of large lizard,
verses.tsw_comparator: These are unclean to you among the swarming creatures that swarm on the ground: the weasel, the mouse, every kind of great lizard,

verses.rationale: Keeps all five source terms separately and in order, with provisional species labels and no collapse into a generic lizard list.
verses.before: the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
verses.after: the gecko, the monitor lizard, the common lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
verses.tsw_comparator: the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.

verses.rationale: Preserves dead-state condition and evening endpoint, distinguishing living species from carcass transmission.
verses.before: These are unclean to you among all the swarming creatures. Whoever touches them when they are dead will be unclean until evening.
verses.after: These are unclean to you among the swarming creatures. Anyone who touches them when they are dead will be unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are unclean to you among all the swarming creatures. Whoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Retains all four material categories, functional scope, immersion and time before clean status rather than washing as immediate restoration.
verses.before: Anything on which one of them falls when dead will become unclean, whether an article of wood, clothing, skin, sackcloth, or any article used for work. It will be put into water and remain unclean until evening; then it will be clean.
verses.after: Anything one of them falls on when dead becomes unclean—a wooden utensil, clothing, leather, or sackcloth, any article used for work. It must be put in water and remain unclean until evening; then it will be clean.
verses.tsw_comparator: Anything on which one of them falls when dead shall become unclean, whether an article of wood, clothing, skin, sackcloth, or any article used for work. It shall be put into water and remain unclean until evening; then it shall be clean.

verses.rationale: Keeps interior contamination and destructive pottery rule, distinct from water treatment of other articles.
verses.before: If any of them falls into an earthen vessel, everything in it will become unclean, and you will break the vessel.
verses.after: If one of them falls into an earthenware vessel, everything inside becomes unclean, and you must break the vessel.
verses.tsw_comparator: If any of them falls into an earthen vessel, everything in it shall become unclean, and you shall break the vessel.

verses.rationale: Makes contaminated-vessel context explicit to avoid claiming all wetted food unclean, retaining food/drink distinction.
verses.before: Any food that may be eaten, if water from such a vessel comes upon it, will become unclean; and any drink that may be drunk from such a vessel will become unclean.
verses.after: Any food in it that has come into contact with water becomes unclean, and any drink in such a vessel becomes unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: Any food that may be eaten, if water from such a vessel comes upon it, shall become unclean; and any drink that may be drunk from such a vessel shall become unclean.

verses.rationale: Retains both cooking installations, dismantling and repeated uncleanness without inserting a hygienic rationale.
verses.before: Anything on which part of their carcass falls will become unclean. An oven or cooking stove will be broken down. They are unclean and will remain unclean to you.
verses.after: Anything on which any part of their carcass falls becomes unclean. An oven or cooking stove must be broken down. They are unclean and must be regarded as unclean by you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Anything on which part of their carcass falls shall become unclean. An oven or cooking stove shall be broken down. They are unclean and shall remain unclean to you.

verses.rationale: Preserves clean water-source exception alongside continuing personal contact impurity.
verses.before: Even so, a spring or cistern collecting water will remain clean, though whoever touches the carcass in it will become unclean.
verses.after: A spring or cistern that holds water, however, remains clean. But anyone who touches the carcass becomes unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nevertheless, a spring or cistern collecting water shall remain clean, though whoever touches the carcass in it shall become unclean.

verses.rationale: Keeps sowing-seed exception and partial-carcass scope without importing the next verse’s water condition.
verses.before: If part of their carcass falls on seed intended for sowing, the seed remains clean.
verses.after: If any part of their carcass falls on seed intended for sowing, the seed remains clean.
verses.tsw_comparator: If part of their carcass falls on seed intended for sowing, the seed remains clean.

verses.rationale: Preserves wet-seed contrast and repeated carcass condition rather than treating all seed identically.
verses.before: But if water has been put on the seed and part of their carcass falls on it, it is unclean to you.
verses.after: But if water has been put on the seed and any part of their carcass falls on it, it is unclean to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if water has been put on the seed and part of their carcass falls on it, it is unclean to you.

verses.rationale: Retains clean edible species becoming source of carcass impurity and exact duration.
verses.before: If any animal that you may eat dies, whoever touches its carcass will be unclean until evening.
verses.after: If an animal you are permitted to eat dies, anyone who touches its carcass will be unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: If any animal that you may eat dies, whoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Preserves distinct eating and carrying cases with full repeated washing/time requirements.
verses.before: Whoever eats from its carcass will wash their clothes and be unclean until evening; whoever carries its carcass will wash their clothes and be unclean until evening.
verses.after: Anyone who eats some of its carcass must wash their clothes and remain unclean until evening. Anyone who carries its carcass must also wash their clothes and remain unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever eats from its carcass shall wash their clothes and be unclean until evening; whoever carries its carcass shall wash their clothes and be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated swarm/ground language and explicit prohibition as the category summary.
verses.before: Every swarming creature that swarms on the ground is detestable; it will not be eaten.
verses.after: Every swarming creature that swarms on the ground is detestable; it must not be eaten.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every swarming creature that swarms on the ground is detestable; it shall not be eaten.

verses.rationale: Keeps belly/four/many-leg categories and judgment; exact source record includes large-letter annotation.
verses.before: Whatever moves on its belly, whatever walks on four legs, or whatever has many feet, among all swarming creatures that swarm on the ground, you will not eat, for they are detestable.
verses.after: Do not eat any creature that swarms on the ground and moves on its belly, goes on all fours, or has many legs. They are detestable.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whatever moves on its belly, whatever walks on four legs, or whatever has many feet, among all swarming creatures that swarm on the ground, you shall not eat, for they are detestable.

verses.rationale: Preserves both detestable and unclean terms and repeated uncleanness without reducing to a single generic warning.
verses.before: You will not make yourselves detestable with any swarming creature, and you will not make yourselves unclean by them and so become defiled by them.
verses.after: Do not make yourselves detestable through any swarming creature. Do not make yourselves unclean through them and so become unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not make yourselves detestable with any swarming creature, and you shall not make yourselves unclean by them and so become defiled by them.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine identity, consecration, holiness grounded in God and repeated ground-creature prohibition.
verses.before: For I am the LORD your God. Make yourselves holy and be holy, for I am holy. You will not make yourselves unclean by any swarming creature that moves on the ground.
verses.after: For I am the LORD your God. Consecrate yourselves and be holy, because I am holy. Do not make yourselves unclean through any swarming creature that crawls on the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I am the LORD your God. Make yourselves holy and be holy, for I am holy. You shall not make yourselves unclean by any swarming creature that moves on the ground.

verses.rationale: Retains upward exodus image, divine purpose and full repeated holiness refrain connecting law to deliverance.
verses.before: For I am the LORD who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God. Therefore you will be holy, for I am holy.
verses.after: For I am the LORD who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God. Be holy, because I am holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I am the LORD who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God. Therefore you shall be holy, for I am holy.

verses.rationale: Preserves four summary groups and living scope, carrying sentence into purpose clause.
verses.before: This is the law concerning animals, birds, every living creature that moves in the waters, and every creature that swarms on the ground,
verses.after: These are the instructions concerning land animals, flying creatures, every living creature that moves in the water, and every creature that swarms on the ground,
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the law concerning animals, birds, every living creature that moves in the waters, and every creature that swarms on the ground,

verses.rationale: Keeps paired distinctions and teaching purpose tied to 10:10, completing the chapter’s speech.
verses.before: to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creature that may be eaten and the living creature that may not be eaten.
verses.after: so that you can distinguish the unclean from the clean, and the animals that may be eaten from those that must not be eaten.”
verses.tsw_comparator: to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creature that may be eaten and the living creature that may not be eaten.

verses.rationale: Preserves fresh speech and Moses-only recipient after joint address in chapter 11.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains conception, male birth, exactly seven days and menstrual-impurity comparison without alleging moral wrongdoing.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: If a woman conceives and gives birth to a male child, she will be unclean seven days; as in the days of the uncleanness of her menstrual period, she will be unclean.
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: When a woman conceives and gives birth to a boy, she will be unclean for seven days, as she is during her menstrual period.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: If a woman conceives and gives birth to a male child, she shall be unclean seven days; as in the days of the uncleanness of her menstrual period, she shall be unclean.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact eighth day and concrete bodily circumcision requirement rather than reducing it to generic dedication.
verses.before: On the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin will be circumcised.
verses.after: On the eighth day, his foreskin must be circumcised.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.

verses.rationale: Preserves thirty-three days, blood connection and both holy-object/sanctuary restrictions; notes difficult bloods-of-purification phrase.
verses.before: She will remain thirty-three days in the blood of purification. She will not touch any holy thing or enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.
verses.after: She must then spend thirty-three days in purification from her bleeding. She must not touch anything holy or enter the sanctuary until her days of purification are complete.
verses.tsw_comparator: She shall remain thirty-three days in the blood of purification. She shall not touch any holy thing or enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.

verses.rationale: Keeps female birth’s distinct two-week and sixty-six-day durations without supplying an explanation absent from source.
verses.before: If she gives birth to a female child, she will be unclean two weeks, as during her menstrual period, and she will remain sixty-six days in the blood of purification.
verses.after: If she gives birth to a girl, she will be unclean for two weeks, as during her menstrual period. Then she must spend sixty-six days in purification from her bleeding.
verses.tsw_comparator: If she gives birth to a female child, she shall be unclean two weeks, as during her menstrual period, and she shall remain sixty-six days in the blood of purification.

verses.rationale: Retains son/daughter coverage, one-year lamb, alternate bird species, differing offering categories and priest/location.
verses.before: When the days of her purification are completed, whether for a son or for a daughter, she will bring to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or turtledove for a sin offering.
verses.after: When her days of purification for a son or daughter are complete, she must bring the priest a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or turtledove for a sin offering, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the days of her purification are completed, whether for a son or for a daughter, she shall bring to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or turtledove for a sin offering.

verses.rationale: Keeps presentation, atonement and cleanness without adding forgiveness of a sin not named; preserves both birth categories in summary.
verses.before: The priest will present them before the LORD and make atonement for her, and she will be clean from the flow of her blood. This is the law for the woman who gives birth to a male or a female child.
verses.after: The priest will present the offering before the LORD and make atonement for her, and she will be clean from her flow of blood. This is the instruction for a woman who gives birth to a boy or a girl.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall present them before the LORD and make atonement for her, and she shall be clean from the flow of her blood. This is the law for the woman who gives birth to a male or a female child.

verses.rationale: Keeps economic accommodation, exactly two birds and separate offering roles; lamb follows prescribed animal in verse 6 and clean conclusion remains distinct from forgiven.
verses.before: If she cannot afford a sheep, she will take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. The priest will make atonement for her, and she will be clean.”
verses.after: If she cannot afford a lamb, she must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering. The priest will make atonement for her, and she will be clean.”
verses.tsw_comparator: If she cannot afford a sheep, she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.”

comparative_references.scope: Supplemental lexical and grammatical comparison. All pinned Hebrew records were read first. Selected chapter-11 lexical notes were consulted before drafting and further grammatical notes afterward; chapter-12 notes were consulted after drafting. English was composed from Hebrew, not by modifying a comparator. Speculative harmonizations and biological rationales are not adopted.

Selected chapter-11 lexical notes were consulted before drafting and further grammatical notes afterward; chapter-12 notes were consulted after drafting. English was composed from Hebrew, not by modifying a comparator. Speculative harmonizations and biological rationales are not adopted.
All 55 Leviticus 11–12 verses read after drafting independently from the pinned Hebrew.
